attempts.error: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired at 2026-09-04T13:57:09.013000+00:00

diagnosis.summary: The attempt never reached a stable 3-node baseline, let alone added node4. The executor spent the whole session in a crash-loop: SST/joiner failures on node1-node3 triggered repeated kill -9 of mariadbd/rsync, then a full wipe and reinstall of /var/lib/mysql on all three nodes, followed by a synchronous restart of all three that failed to form a Primary Component. The lease expired mid-debug with no evidence node4 was ever provisioned or joined.

evidence.finding: An SST (rsync) was in progress with node2 as joiner; state transfer was required because node2's local state was uninitialized (00000000-...:-1) against group state at seqno 4.
Executor killed mariadbd/wsrep_sst_rsync/rsync at least 6 times across node1 and node2, indicating repeated stuck or failed state-transfer attempts rather than a single isolated failure.
Executor ran `rm -rf /var/lib/mysql` followed by `mariadb-install-db` on all three nodes - a full data wipe and reinitialization on every member, not just the problem node.

wsrep_cluster_address was already set to 'gcomm://node1,node2,node3,node4' - including node4 - before any evidence in the record that node4 was provisioned, started, or had mariadb installed. No command in the entire selected audit targets node4.

All three nodes were launched as background jobs within about 1 second of each other, with none using bootstrap syntax (empty gcomm:// or --wsrep-new-cluster); each pointed at the same 4-node gcomm address list including node4.

Views formed showing 2 then 3 real members present, but each view was logged as NON_PRIM with 'no nodes coming from prim view, prim not possible' - i.e. even once all three live nodes saw each other, Galera would not elect a Primary Component.
gcs.cpp gcs_open() failed: "Failed to open channel 'galera_cluster' at 'gcomm://node1,node2,node3,node4': -110 (Operation timed out)"; wsrep::connect failed: 7; mariadbd aborted.

Attempt to set up passwordless inter-node SSH failed: '~/.ssh/id_ed25519: No such file or directory' (no ~/.ssh dir created first) and subsequent ssh calls returned 'Permission denied (publickey,password,keyboard-interactive)'.

197 of 198 requested commands completed; only a curated subset of 31 records (recent failures/successes) was provided, so some intermediate diagnostic steps and any node4-specific commands may be omitted from what's shown, though none appear in the selection.

likely_causes.cause: Fresh-cluster restart never used a bootstrap step (empty gcomm:// or --wsrep-new-cluster) on any node; all three nodes were started concurrently pointing at a full 4-member gcomm list, so Galera had no way to elect an initial Primary Component even after all three came up.
wsrep_cluster_address on node1 already listed node4 before node4 existed/joined; gcs attempted to resolve/connect to it and timed out (-110), compounding the quorum failure.

The original SST/joiner failures that triggered the crash-loop were never root-caused before the executor escalated to destructive recovery (wiping and reinstalling datadirs on all three nodes), which both destroyed application data the task required node4 to inherit and reset the cluster into the harder 'bootstrap from nothing' scenario.

Inter-node SSH via the cluster keypair was never functional (missing ~/.ssh directory before writing the key), which may have blocked any node4-side orchestration or cross-node file transfer the executor intended to use.

next_attempt_guidance: Bring up the 3-node cluster in the correct bootstrap sequence: start node1 alone with an empty/bootstrap gcomm address (or `mysqld --wsrep-new-cluster`) so it forms its own Primary Component, confirm wsrep_cluster_size=1 and wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, then start node2 and node3 one at a time (not concurrently) each pointing at the full existing-node gcomm list, verifying SST/IST completes and cluster_size increments before starting the next.

Do not add node4 to wsrep_cluster_address on any existing node until the 3-node cluster is confirmed healthy (Primary, size 3, all synced). Only then provision node4, install mariadb, set its own gcomm address to include all four nodes, update the other three nodes' configs to include node4, and start node4 last.

If a joiner's SST hangs or a node crashes, diagnose with `tail -f /var/log/messages` and `ps aux` before killing processes; avoid `rm -rf /var/lib/mysql` on healthy donor nodes - a wipe should be scoped to the single broken joiner, never applied to all members, since it destroys the application data the task requires preserving.

Before relying on inter-node SSH, run `mkdir -p ~/.ssh && chmod 700 ~/.ssh` before writing CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY into it; verify with a simple `ssh node2 echo ok` early, independent of any Galera troubleshooting.

After each node start, don't just trust `rc-service mariadb status`; that command can lag behind an actual crash. Poll `mysql -u root -e "show status like 'wsrep_cluster_status'"` and check the return code/error text directly, and inspect /var/log/messages for 'Aborting' or NON_PRIM view lines before proceeding to the next node.

Since this evidence comes from a curated subset of 31 of 395 records with no node4 activity visible at all, treat 'node4 was never provisioned' as the working assumption but confirm this is not an artifact of record selection if further logs become available.
